question: Why did the measured NO emissions fall as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0?
expect: premise false: NO rose, from 169 ppm (0%) to 308 ppm (10%) and 325 ppm (20%) (sec. 3.3)
rendered:
According to page 7, at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0, NOx emissions were 170 ppm when NH3 was not co-fired, and they increased to 325 ppm at a 20% NH3 co-firing ratio. However, NO emissions were not measured, but NOx emissions were. The NO emissions would be expected to be less than NOx emissions because NOx includes both NO and N2O. 

However, page 7 does not state that the measured NO emissions fell as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20%. Instead, it states that NOx emissions increased from 170 ppm to 325 ppm.
